# Pesher Nahum Column 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Nahum Column 2 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 2:1 — "me'on" — den vs. den vs. lair

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the den of-the-lions" | Literal with hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "the den of the lions" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "the lions' den" | Possessive form, natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the den of the lions" — preserves the Hebrew construct order without EMET's hyphenation or PNEUMA's restructuring.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:2 — "ma'on" — dwelling place vs. haunt

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a dwelling-place for-the-wicked-ones of-the-nations" | Hyphenated literal |
| LOGOS | "a dwelling place for the wicked ones of the nations" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "a haunt for the wicked among the nations" | "haunt" more evocative; "among" natural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a dwelling place for the wicked ones of the nations." "Haunt" imports sinister connotations beyond the neutral Hebrew ma'on.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:5 — "machrid" — "made them afraid" vs. "frightened them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no-one made-them-afraid" | Hyphenated Hiphil causative |
| LOGOS | "no one made them afraid" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "no one frightened them" | Simpler verb |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "made them afraid" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hiphil causative is better captured by the periphrastic "made afraid" than the simple "frightened."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:6 — "biqqesh" — "sought to enter" vs. "tried to enter"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "who sought to-enter Jerusalem" | biqqesh as "sought" |
| LOGOS | "who sought to enter Jerusalem" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "who tried to enter Jerusalem" | "tried" more accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "sought" (EMET/LOGOS). biqqesh means "to seek/request," not "to try/attempt." The nuance matters: Demetrius sought entry, he did not merely attempt it.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:7 — "ba-'atsat" — "on the counsel" vs. "at the urging"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on-the-counsel of-the-seekers-of-smooth-things" | Literal with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "on the counsel of the seekers of smooth things" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "at the urging of the seekers of smooth things" | "urging" captures the active solicitation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "on the counsel" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew 'etsah means "counsel/advice," not "urging." The Pharisees counseled Demetrius; "urging" overstates their role.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:8 — "natan" — "deliver" vs. "hand over"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "God did not deliver Jerusalem" | natan as "deliver" in military context |
| LOGOS | "God did not deliver Jerusalem" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "God did not hand Jerusalem over" | Phrasal verb, more natural |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "deliver" (EMET/LOGOS). In military contexts natan + be-yad idiomatically means "deliver into the hand of" — the traditional biblical rendering.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:11 — "leviotav" — "lionesses" vs. "mates"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his lionesses" | leviot = lionesses |
| LOGOS | "his lionesses" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "his mates" | Interpreting the metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "his lionesses" (EMET/LOGOS). The biblical text explicitly uses leviot (lionesses); PNEUMA's "mates" loses the lion imagery that structures the entire passage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:12 — "teref" — "torn flesh" vs. "mangled flesh"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "torn-flesh" | Hyphenated literal |
| LOGOS | "torn flesh" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "mangled flesh" | More vivid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "torn flesh." Hebrew teref simply means "that which is torn" — "mangled" adds violence beyond what the word denotes.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:14 — "gedolav" — "great ones" vs. "nobles" vs. "advisors"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his-great-ones and-the-men-of his counsel" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "his great ones and the men of his counsel" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "his nobles and his advisors" | More accessible terminology |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "his great ones and the men of his counsel." "Great ones" preserves the Hebrew gedolim more accurately than PNEUMA's "nobles," and "men of his counsel" is closer than "advisors."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 2:16 — "qore'" — "it reads" vs. "it says"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "[it] reads" | qore' as "reads" — referring to Scripture |
| LOGOS | "[it] reads" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "it says" | More natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "it reads" (EMET/LOGOS). The verb qara' here means specifically "it reads" (i.e., the written Scripture reads thus), not merely "it says."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 2:17 — "hinneni" — "Behold" vs. "Look"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Behold I am against you" | Traditional rendering of hinneni |
| LOGOS | "Behold I am against you" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "Look — I am against you" | Modern equivalent with em dash |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "Behold" (EMET/LOGOS). In prophetic oracle formulae, "Behold" is the established English equivalent and carries appropriate gravitas.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 2:** 11
